newsitem.title: RUSSIA: British Gas' Russian oil joint venture boosts '96 output.
newsitem.headline: British Gas' Russian oil joint venture boosts '96 output.

text.p: Russian oil firm KomArcticOil, a joint venture between British Gas Plc and Russian oil company KomiTEK, produced 1.13 million tonnes of oil in 1996, up 41 percent from 1995 levels, the venture said in a statement.
It said it was the first time over the venture's five year history that annual output exceeded one million tonnes.
The venture sold 1.01 million tonnes of crude oil last year, but it was unclear what amount of the oil was exported outside the Commonwealth of Independent States.
KomiArcticOil exploits a section of the Vozeisk oil reserves in the Arctic Komi Republic.
The company has produced a total of 3.7 million tonnes of oil since it was set up in 1992.
It has spent $229 million on capital expenditure, paid $106 million into various budgets and given $2.0 million to social development programs in the Komi region, the release said.
KomiArcticOil was involved in the clean-up of one of Russia's worst recorded oil spills caused by a rupture to a nearby pipeline.
KomiArcticOil's main production unit is Komineft.
